guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why the market is willing to price Oregon State aggressively. Braden Atkinson has surpassed 300 passing yards in all four games, while Jesse Legree has opened the season with four consecutive 100-yard receiving performances. We are not dismissing that explosiveness, but our numbers distinguish between piling up passing yards and consistently creating scoring opportunities. That is where Washington State’s defense matches up better than the headline production suggests. Oregon State has converted every red-zone trip, but our view is that getting into scoring position often enough remains the more important question.

The concern for us is Washington State’s offense. It has converted only 28.9 percent of its third downs, and its inefficient passing game now faces an Oregon State defense averaging 3.5 sacks per game. That creates real risk of stalled possessions and poor field position. Still, Caden Pinnick offers an important counter with his mobility: through four games, he had 201 rushing yards and 13 runs of at least 10 yards.

For us, the case is less about Washington State matching Oregon State’s passing production and more about whether Oregon State can turn its yardage advantage into enough separation. Our model is skeptical because Washington State’s defensive profile is stronger in the areas that limit scoring opportunities, while Oregon State’s rushing efficiency has not provided the same consistent support as its passing game.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Washington State’s pass protection against Oregon State’s pressure. Washington State allowed six sacks against Arizona, and Oregon State recorded eight against UTEP. If Oregon State repeatedly creates negative plays, Washington State’s offensive limitations become much harder to overcome.

Pinnick’s ability to escape pressure matters here. We do not need Washington State to win the passing matchup outright, but we do need it to avoid giving Oregon State extra possessions and short fields. If Pinnick can turn some pressure into positive runs, Washington State has a better path to sustaining enough offense for our position.

recent_game.fact: Washington State lost 34-24 to Arizona on September 26, falling to 1-3.
Washington State produced 335 total yards against Arizona, with 241 passing yards and 94 rushing yards, while allowing 447 total yards.
Washington State led Arizona 14-0 in the first quarter and 17-14 at halftime but was outscored 20-7 after halftime.
Washington State converted 5 of 15 third downs, allowed six sacks and committed two turnovers against Arizona.

opponent_notes.fact: Washington State is scheduled to play at Oregon State on October 17, 2026 at 3 p.m. Pacific in a Pac-12 game.
Oregon State was 2-2 overall and 0-0 in Pac-12 play when this guide was issued.

quarterback.fact: Redshirt sophomore transfer Caden Pinnick was named Washington State's starting quarterback on August 24.
Pinnick completed 24 of 41 passes for 241 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Arizona while rushing 13 times for 35 yards and a touchdown.
Through four games, Pinnick had 201 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns and owned 13 runs of at least 10 yards.
Pinnick transferred from UC Davis after throwing for 3,206 yards, 32 touchdowns and 10 interceptions and rushing for 437 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

offensive_personnel.fact: Washington State returned four 2025 starters, all on offense: wide receiver Tony Freeman, right tackle Jonny Lester, left tackle Ashton Tripp and running back Kirby Vorhees.
The offensive line against Arizona started Ashton Tripp at left tackle, Jonny Lester at left guard, Noah Dunham at center, Nick Bakken at right guard and Jaylin Caldwell at right tackle.
Tripp started all 13 games at left tackle in 2025 and allowed one sack in 490 pass-blocking snaps.
Dunham moved from left guard to center before 2026 fall camp and has started at center.
Lester started at right tackle in the opener, played right tackle, right guard and left guard at Kansas State, and started the next two games at left guard.
Caldwell played the final 33 snaps at right tackle against Kansas State and started the next two games there.

Against Arizona, Tank Hawkins Jr. caught six passes for 37 yards, Daniel Blood had five catches for 57 yards, Branden Ganashamoorthy had four catches for 67 yards and a touchdown, and Darrius Clemons had four catches for 57 yards.
Washington State's roster included 50 new players, including 29 transfers from four-year schools.

defensive_personnel.fact: Washington State's defensive starters against Arizona were Linus Zunk, Kaden Beatty, Jirah Leaupepetele and Matyus McLain on the line; Keith Brown and DJ Warner at linebacker; Jaylen Thomas at nickel; Khamari Terrell and Jamarey Smith at cornerback; and Jackquintin Bal and Jeremiah Bernard at safety.
Jackquintin Bal made a career-high nine tackles and returned his first career interception 25 yards for a touchdown against Arizona.
Linus Zunk recorded five tackles and two sacks against Arizona.
Matyus McLain made a career-high eight tackles and shared a sack against Arizona.
Keith Brown made a career-high eight tackles, DJ Warner made a career-high seven tackles and Jamarey Smith made a career-high seven tackles against Arizona.
Jaylen Thomas had two interceptions, including a 50-yard touchdown return, against Kansas State and was named Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Week.

coaching_changes.fact: Kirby Moore was named Washington State head coach on December 12, 2025 and is in his first season leading the Cougars.
Matt Miller is the first-year offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Trent Bray is the first-year defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.

Jack Abercrombie is the first-year offensive line coach, Derek Sage is the first-year wide receivers coach and special-teams coordinator, and Justin Green is the first-year assistant head coach and running backs coach.
Miller works from the booth, while Moore is listed on the field.

injury_availability.fact: Cornerback Jalil Tucker, an Oregon State transfer, had missed the previous three games with an injury after starting the season opener.
Cornerback Khamari Terrell missed the Kansas State game with an injury but returned to start against Duquesne and made four tackles with one pass breakup against Arizona.
Tight end Trey Leckner had not played in the first four games of 2026.
Right guard Nick Bakken missed most of 2025 with an injury but started each of Washington State's first four games in 2026.
Right tackle Jaylin Caldwell missed the remainder of the 2025 season after two starts because of injury and had started Washington State's two most recent games in 2026.

recent_game.fact: Oregon State defeated UTEP 33-7 on Sept. 26 to improve to 2-2.
